newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi oil firm still backs Afghan export projects.
newsitem.headline: Saudi oil firm still backs Afghan export projects.

text.p: Jeddah-based Delta Oil was still committed to two Central Asian oil and gas projects planned to pass through war-torn Afghanistan to reach world markets, the English language Saudi Gazette newspaper reported on Monday.
"We are ready and totally equipped, as soon as the Afghanistan conflict is over. We are ready to wait for this project," Yasir Niazi, a Delta spokesman told the paper.

Delta has tied up with U.S. Unocal Corp to build a natural gas pipeline that would carry some two billion cubic feet a day of gas from Turkmenistan's Dauletabad field across Afghanistan to power stations in Pakistan.
The project would take one year to complete after the start of work, Niazi told the paper.
It also aims to construct a 1,700-km pipeline to carry a million barrels per day (bpd) of crude from the Chardzhou field to an export terminal on Pakistan's Arabian Sea coast.
Fighting has continued between the Islamist Taleban militia and government forces who were ousted from Kabul in September.
Unocal Pakistan Ltd president and general manager Richard Keller in October said that Unocal remained committed to the trans-Afghan projects. -- Steven Swindells, Dubai Newsroom, +971 4 6071255
